description.value: Relationships between episodic memory, brain microstructure measured by diffusion tensor imaging, and grey matter volumes measured by voxel-based morphometry were investigated in detoxified alcoholics and healthy men.

spans.text: Diffusion and morphometric analyses were performed in 24 alcohol dependent men without neurological or somatic complications and in 24 healthy men.

value: We hypothesized that microstructural changes in temporal, parahippocampal and hippocampal areas, more than volumetric changes in these regions or elsewhere in the brain, could be related to episodic memory impairment.
We hypothesized that the ADC values in temporal regions would account for the verbal memory performance in alcoholics.

description.value: Cross-sectional comparison of 24 alcohol dependent men and 24 healthy men, with voxel-based diffusion and morphometric imaging analyses and memory-performance regressions.

spans.text: Participants were 24 patients who met DSM-IV criteria for alcohol dependence and 24 healthy participants.

definition.value: Between-group comparisons of ADC showed significant clusters with increased ADC in alcoholics mainly in temporal and frontal regions and in the cerebellum.

spans.text: All regression analyses were carried out with an exploratory uncorrected statistical threshold set at   p  <0.001 with a minimal cluster size of 10 voxels.

value: Between-group comparisons of ADC showed significant clusters with increased ADC in alcoholics mainly in temporal and frontal regions and in the cerebellum.
Alcoholics had widespread increase of ADC in multiple brain regions. Higher ADC was found mainly in frontal and temporal regions and in the cerebellum.

definition.value: Between-group comparisons of the grey matter volumes showed volume decreases in alcoholics compared to healthy subjects.

spans.text: All regression analyses were carried out with an exploratory uncorrected statistical threshold set at   p  <0.001 with a minimal cluster size of 10 voxels.

value: Whereas smaller volumes in alcoholics were revealed in brain regions where ADC was higher in these participants, no significant correlation was found between brain region volumes and free recall scores in alcohol dependent group.
Alcoholics had lower grey matter volumes in all of these regions.

value: Regional regression analysis between memory performance and ADC in alcoholics revealed negative correlations bilaterally in the hippocampus and parahippocampus gyri, bilaterally in the middle frontal gyri, and in the left superior temporal gyri.
Higher microscopic water diffusion in these brain regions is associated with degraded memory performance.

definition.value: The semantic performance (WAIS-information) was correlated with ADC values.

spans.text: The semantic performance (WAIS-information) was correlated with ADC values in left (x = −44; y = 27; z = −16) and right (x = 30; y = 33; z = 0) frontal regions.
All regression analyses were carried out with an exploratory uncorrected statistical threshold set at   p  <0.001 with a minimal cluster size of 10 voxels.

Also, the between-group comparison of semantic performance indicated significant effect of group on WAIS-information scores (  sum Z-Scores  : Alcoholics: −1.7±1.39; Controls: 0.03±1.37; t (44) = −4.23; p<0.001).

value: The semantic performance (WAIS-information) was correlated with ADC values in left and right frontal regions.
ADC abnormalities in cortical regions underlie semantic memory impairment.
